newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS ON BRINK OF ITALIAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS ON BRINK OF ITALIAN TITLE.

text.p: Champions Cup finalists Juventus need only a point from their Friday evening league game at Atalanta to clinch their 24th Italian title.

With two Serie A games to play, Juventus have a six-point lead over second-placed Parma and can wrap up the trophy before Wednesday's Champions Cup final against German side Borussia Dortmund in Munich.
Even if Juventus were to lose on Friday, they could still theoretically win the title this weekend if Parma fail to win against Bologna on Sunday.
Mercurial Juventus schemer Alessandro Del Piero, who is expected to play against Atalanta, concedes the players already have Wednesday's final on their minds when playing against Atalanta.
"Myself, I just want us to wrap up this league title and I'm focussed on that.
"But it's only normal, even inevitable that your thoughts race forward five days to Munich.
"Still we all know how important it is on Friday because we can settle the whole league title business there and then."
Del Piero, just back from injury, has played only 10 full league games in a season which has seen him ruled out for 77 days by injury.
A draw seems a likely result in Bergamo on Friday since home side Atalanta need only one point to be certain of avoiding relegation.
Atalanta are currently 12th on 40 points, six points clear of the three relegation battlers Cagliari, Piacenza and Perugia, all on 34.
Atalanta coach Emilio Mondonico reckons his side deserve plaudits too for a successful season which sees striker Filippo Inzaghi currently leading the Serie A goalscorers' chart with 21.

"Juventus just have to be their normal selves to win the title, whilst we had to pull off a great feat never before seen by our fans in order to win our title, that is Pippo Inzaghi as the leading goalscorer.
"Juventus might be the strongest side in the world but in this championship they have not faced serious competition.

"Second-placed Parma were in the relegation zone a third of the way through the season whilst third place Inter are getting rid of their coach (Englishman Roy Hodgson) because no one is happy with the way he gets the team to play."

Juventus will be without two suspended players on Friday. Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero and utility player Sergio Porrini are set to be replaced by Mark Juliano and Alessio Tacchinardi respectively.
In attack, Christian Vieri will partner Del Piero while Atillio Lombardo replaces Angelo Di Livio in midfield.
Atalanta will be without experienced defender Walter Bonacina, who is suspended, but field their customary three-man attack of Domenico Morfeo playing behind Gigi Lentini and Inzaghi.
